shalt receive them of their hands, and burn <hi type="italic">them </hi>upon the altar for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour before the LORD: it <hi type="italic">is </hi>an offering made by fire unto the LORD.<div eID="gen11695" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen11696" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25.</hi> Accipies autem illa e manu eorum, et incendes super altare, ultra holocaustum in eID="gen11698" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen11699" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">27.</hi> And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave sID="gen11701" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28.</hi> And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’ by a statute for ever from the children of Israel: for it <hi type="italic">is </hi>an heave offering: and it </cell><cell> <div sID="gen11702" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">28.</hi> Et erit ipsi Aharon et filiis ejus in statutum perpetuum a filiis Israel: quia exaltatio est: et exaltatio erit a filiis Israel </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen11705" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">30.</hi> <hi type="italic">And </hi>that son that is priest in his stead shall put them on seven days, when he cometh into the <div sID="gen11707" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">31.</hi> And thou shalt take the ram of the consecration, and seethe his flesh in the holy place.<div eID="gen11707" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen11708" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">31.</hi> Arietem autem consecrationum tolles, et coques carnem ejus in loco sanctitatis.<div eID="gen11708" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen11709" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">32.</hi> And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that <hi type="italic">is </hi>in the basket, <hi type="italic">by </hi>the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.<div eID="gen11709" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen11710" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">32.</hi> Comedetque Aharon et filii ejus carnem arietis, et type="italic">are </hi>holy.<div eID="gen11711" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen11712" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">33.</hi> Comedent inquam illa quibus expiatus fuit ad consecrandum manum sID="gen11716" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">35.</hi> Facies igitur ipsi Aharon et filiis ejus sic, juxta omnia quae praecepi tibi: septem diebus consecrabis manum eorum.<div eID="gen11716" type="x-p"/> <ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="28" type="chapter">
                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXVIII.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 AND take thou unto thee <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Cause them to come near unto thee, that thou maist be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore them and before the people declare the will of God here<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in, and solemnly set them apart for this office.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Heb. 5. 1, 4.</ns0:note> Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ster unto me in the priests office, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> Aaron, Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dab and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, Aarons sons.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 39. 2.</ns0:note> thou shalt make <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>an holy stole.</ns0:hi> Rev. 7. 9.</ns0:note> holy garments <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Garments to be used onely in holy ministrations.</ns0:note> for Aaron thy brother, for glory and for beauty <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Such as are glorious and beautiful, partly to mind the people of the dignity and excellency of their office and employment, and principally to represent the glorious robes wherewith Christ is both clothed himself and clotheth all his people, who are made Priests unto God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 36. 1.</ns0:note> thou shalt speak unto all that are wise<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hearted <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Skilful artists. The Hebrews make the heart, not the brain, the seat of wisdome. See <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 9. 4.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 31. 2. and 35. 30.</ns0:note> whom I have filled <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Either 1. by my ordinary providence and assistance, giving them both ability and opportunity to learn the arts: or rather 2. by extraordinary inspiration, which was necessary for the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> whose base and laborious drudgery took off their minds and hands from all in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />genious studies and arts.</ns0:note> with the spirit of wisdom, that they make Aarons garments to consecrate him <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) To be an outward sign of my calling and consecration of him to my holy service. A me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tonymical expression.</ns0:note>, that he may minister unto me in the priests office.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And these <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the garments which they shall make; a breast-plate, and an ephod <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">This was a short upper garment, made without sleeves, which was girt about the body. And it was twofold, the one made of fine linnen, which was common not onely to all the Priests, as 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2. 18. and 22. 18. but to some others also upon solemn and sacred occasions, as 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 6. 14. the other made of divers stuffes and colours, peculiar to the High-priest, the parts whereof were not sewed, but tied together.</ns0:note>, and a robe <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">An upper garment, like a surpliss.</ns0:note>, and a broidered coat <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">An under coat curiously wrought with circular works like eyes, as the word notes, and richly adorned with gems and other things.</ns0:note>, a mitre <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">A kind of bon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />net or cap for the covering of the head, supposed to be some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing like a <ns0:hi>Turkish</ns0:hi> Turband for the form of it.</ns0:note>, and a girdle <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">To enclose and fasten all the other garments, which were loose in them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves, that he might be more expeditious in his work.</ns0:note>: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nister unto me in the priests office.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And they shall take gold, and blue, and pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, and scarlet, and fine linen.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And they shall make the ephod <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> gold <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Beaten out into plates and cut into wires.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> blue, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> purple, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> scarlet, and fine twined linen, <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> cunning work.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 It shall have the two shoulder-pieces <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Which were two parts of the Ephod going up from the body of<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> the Ephod, the one before, the other behind, which when the Priest had put over his head, were tied together and covered the Priests shoulders and part of his back and breast.</ns0:note> there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />of joyned at the two edges thereof; and so it shall be joyned together.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> embroi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dered.</ns0:note> curious girdle of the ephod <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Which was for the closer fastening and girding of it.</ns0:note> which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> upon it <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">This is added to distinguish it from the other girdle <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 4. which was to gird all the garments, and was tied in a lower place.</ns0:note>; shall be of the same <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Either 1. of the same piece: or rather 2. of the same kind of materials and workmanship, as the following words explain it.</ns0:note>, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the work thereof, <ns0:hi>even of</ns0:hi> gold, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 Six of their names on one stone, and <ns0:hi>the other six</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Levi</ns0:hi> seems to be omitted here, as being sufficiently repre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sented by the High-priest himself.</ns0:note> names of the rest on the other stone, according to their birth:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Wisd. 18<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note> With the work of an engraver in stone, <ns0:hi>like the</ns0:hi> engravings of a signet shalt thou engrave the two stones, with the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be set in ouches <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Hollow places, such as are made in golden rings to receive and hold the precious stones, which are put into them.</ns0:note> of gold.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And thou shalt put the two stones upon the shoulders of the ephod <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) In the place where the two shoulder-pieces were joyned together.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> stones of memorial unto the children of Israel. And Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Into the holy of holies. An evident type of Christs entring into heaven with the names and in the stead of his people, the true <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> upon his shoulders, and present<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them to his father with acceptance.</ns0:note>, upon his two shoulders for a memorial <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Not so much to the High-priest, that he should not forget to pray for them, as to God, that he, beholding their names there according to his or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der, might graciously remember them and shew mercy unto them. Such a memorial to God was the rainbow, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 9. 13. Such things are spoken of God after the manner of men.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And thou shalt make ouches <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Not for the stones, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 12. who had other ouches, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 11. but for the chains, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 14.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> gold:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And two chains <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> pure gold at the ends <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>with ends, (i. e.)</ns0:hi> not like chains that are fastened a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout ones neck or arm, which seem to have no end, but two distinct chains with two several ends, both hanging downward. Compare <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 22. The Syriack render it <ns0:hi>double,</ns0:hi> others <ns0:hi>equal,</ns0:hi> or of equal length.</ns0:note>: <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> wreathen work shalt thou make them, and fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sten the wreathen chains to the ouches.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And thou shalt make the breast-plate of judgement <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This was a square and curiously wrought piece put over the Ephod upon ones breast, called <ns0:hi>of judgment,</ns0:hi> because from thence the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> were to expect and receive their judgment and the mind of God in all those weighty matters of war or peace, wherein they consulted God for direction.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> cunning work, after the work of the ephod thou shalt make it: <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> gold, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> blue, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> purple, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> scarlet, and <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> fine twined linen shalt thou make it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 Four square it shall be, <ns0:hi>being</ns0:hi> doubled <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For greater strength that it might better support and se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cure the precious stones which were put into it, and that it might receive the Urim and Thummim, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 8. 8.</ns0:note>: a span <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> the length thereof, and a span <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> the breadth thereof.</ns0:p>

It may rather seem that these are other chains fastened to the breast<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plate, as it follows, whereas those chains <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 14. seem to have been fastened to the ephod, to those ouches made in it for that purpose, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 13. And whereas these chains also are fastened in the said ouches <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 25. two several chains may well enough be fastened in divers parts of each of the ouches, and there seems to be this difference between the chains, those chains menti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />oned <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 14. are said to be fastened onely at one end, even to the ouches of the Ephod, whence they might hang down loose<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, whereas these are manifestly fastened at both ends, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 24, 25.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> wreathen work <ns0:hi>of</ns0:hi> pure gold.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="25">25 And <ns0:hi>the other</ns0:hi> two ends of the two wreathen <ns0:hi>chains,</ns0:hi> thou shalt fasten in the two ouches, and put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore it <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) In the fore-part of the Ephod: or <ns0:hi>before him, i. e.</ns0:hi> the High-priest, in his fore-part, upon his breast.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 And thou shalt make two rings of gold, and thou shalt put them upon the two ends <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">To wit, upon the lower ends, for there were other rings put upon the upper ends, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 23, 24, 25.</ns0:note> of the breast-plate, in the border thereof, which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in the side of the ephod inward <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) In the inner side of the Ephod, under which these rings were hid: for the Ephod was double, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 16.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 And two other <ns0:hi>rings</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">To answer the two rings in the breast-plate, that by all these the breast-plate might be the better fastened to the Ephod.</ns0:note> of gold thou shalt make, and shalt put them on the two sides of the ephod underneath <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">In the lower part of the ephod, or in that part of it which is under the lowest part of the breast-plate.</ns0:note>, towards the forepart there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />of <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Towards the breast.</ns0:note>, over against the <ns0:hi>other</ns0:hi> coupling thereof <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Over against the ouches on the shoulder-pieces, where the upper part of the breast-plate was fastened to the Ephod.</ns0:note>, above the curious girdle of the ephod.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 And they shall bind the breast-plate by the rings thereof, unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> may be above the curious girdle of the ephod, and that the breast-plate be not loosed from the ephod.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29 And Aaron shall bear the names of the chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren of Israel, in the breast-plate of judgment, upon his heart <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Partly to admonish the High-priest of that dear affection he should have to his people, and with what ardency he should pray for them, and principally to represent the tender compas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sions of Christ, the great high-priest, towards his people, and how mindful he is of them and of all their concerns, even when he is in the holy of holies, that is, in heaven, where he remembers them still and uncessantly intercedes for them.</ns0:note>, when he goeth in unto the holy <ns0:hi>place</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Into the most holy place, the positive degree being put for the superlative.</ns0:note>, for a memorial before the LORD con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tinually.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 33. 8. Ezra 2. 63. Neh. 7. 65.</ns0:note> thou shalt put in the breast-plate of judgement, the Urim and the Thummim <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The words confessedly signify <ns0:hi>light</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>illuminations</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fections</ns0:hi> which may be understood either of two differing things, the one noting the knowledge, the other the perfection, to wit, of vertues and graces, which were required in the High-priest<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and which were in Christ in an eminent degree, and from him alone communicated to his people, or of one and the same thing, noting perfect light or illumination, by a figure called Hendyadis, oft used in Scripture, as <ns0:hi>Deat.</ns0:hi> 16. 18. Mat. 4. 16. compared with <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 10. 20. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3. 5. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 17. 25. compared with <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 2. 7. Which may seem probable, 1. because the great use of this instrument was to give light and direction in dubi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous and difficult cases, and not to confer any other perfection upon any person. 2. because sometimes both these words or things are expressed onely by one of them, and that is by <ns0:hi>Urim, Numb.</ns0:hi> 27. 21. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 28. 6. which signifies <ns0:hi>lights.</ns0:hi> And the name seems to be given from the effect, because hence the <ns0:hi>Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />raelites</ns0:hi> had clear light and perfect or certain direction in dark and doubtful matters. But the great question is, What this Urim and Thummim was, and in what manner God answered by it. Which God having on purpose concealed from us, and not set down the matter or form of it, as he hath done of all the other particulars, it may seem curiosity and presumption for men solicitously to enquire and positively to determine. Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny conceive it was nothing else but the twelve precious stones, wherein the names of the 12 Tribes were engraven, and that the answer of God was composed out of those letters which ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther shew more brightly, or thrust themselves further outward than the rest did. Which seems a frivolous and ungrounded conjecture, both because all the letters of the Alphabet were not there, and so all answers could not be given by them, and be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause it was shut up within the duplicature of the breast-plate, and therefore could not be seen by the High-priest, and there is not a word to signifie that he was to take it out thence and look upon it, but rather the contrary is evident. And that this Urim and Thummim are not the same thing with those 12 stones may be easily proved. 1 because the stones were <ns0:hi>set</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>ingraven</ns0:hi> in the breast-plate, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 17, 21. this was only <ns0:hi>put</ns0:hi> into it, which is a word of quite different and more loose and large signification, and therefore probably doth not design the same thing. 2. It is not likely, that in such a brief account of the sacred utensils, the same command would be repeated again, especially in more dark and general words than it was mentioned before. And how could <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> now put it in, when the workmen had fasten<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed it there before? Or why should he be required to put it in the breast-plate, when it was fastened to it already, and could not without violence be taken from it. 3. because the stones were put in by the workmen, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 39. 10. the Urim and Thummim by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> himself, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 8. 8. It is objected, that where the stones are mentioned, there is no mention of Urim and Thummim, as <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 39. and that where the Urim and Thummim are mentioned, there is no mention of the stones, as <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 8. 8. which shews they were one and the same thing. But that is not necessary<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and there is an evident reason of both those omissions; of the former <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 39. because he mentions onely those things which were made by the workmen, whereas the Urim and Thum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mim seems to have been made immediately by God, or by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> with Gods direction: of the latter <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 8. because the stones are im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plyed in the breast-plate as a part of it and being fastened to it, whereas there he onely mentions what was put in by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> himself. There are other conjectures, as that it was the name Jehovah, or some visible representations, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> But such conjectures are easily denied as affirmed. It is therefore more modest and reason<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />able to be silent where God is silent, than to indulge our selves in boundless and groundless fancies. It may suffice us to know that this was a singular piece of Divine Workmanship, which the High-priest was obliged to wear upon solemn occasions, as one of the conditions upon which God engaged to give him answers. Which answers God might give to him either by in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward suggestion to his mind, or by a vocal expression to his ear. But which of those ways, or whether by any other way, it is needless now to search, and impossible certainly to discover.</ns0:note>, and they shall be upon Aarons heart, when he goeth in before the LORD: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">A short speech. As the <ns0:hi>testimony</ns0:hi> is oft put for the <ns0:hi>ark of the testimony,</ns0:hi> so is the <ns0:hi>judgment</ns0:hi> here for the <ns0:hi>breast-plate of judgment, i. e.</ns0:hi> that breast-plate which declared the judgment or oracle or mind of God to the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> in those cases which they brought to the Lord.</ns0:note> upon his heart, before the LORD continually <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) At all times when he shall appear before the Lord in the holy-place.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Not the Ephod it self, for that was prescribed before <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 6. but a long and loose robe called the <ns0:hi>robe of the Ephod,</ns0:hi> because it was worn next under it, and was girded about the High-priests body with the curious girdle of the Ephod.</ns0:note> all of blue.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="38">38 And it shall be upon Aarons forehead, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Either, 1. that he, being consecrated to God for this end, that he should take care as far as he could that both persons and things presented to God should be holy or agreeable to the mind of God, might bear the punishment for any miscarriage com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mitted therein, which he could have prevented.                         </ns0:gap> of the people, and to inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cede for them might take away, or obtain from God the par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />don of their <ns0:hi>iniquity</ns0:hi> wherewith even their <ns0:hi>holy things</ns0:hi> are de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />filed, if God should severely mark what is amiss in them.
